annotationRationale: The derivation expresses the geometric common ratio in lowest terms, uses integrality to force its numerator and denominator to divide 720, and uses disjoint prime factors to prove minimality.
sourceMethod: Follows the official reduced-common-ratio and prime-factor argument. Clarifies why a smaller ratio forces both numerator and denominator above 17, including the denominator-16 and denominator-17 cases.

review.mathCheck: Writing r = m/n in lowest terms forces both m and n to divide 720. A ratio between 1 and 16/15 requires n > 15; n = 16 and 17 are excluded explicitly. Larger coprime divisors would each require two distinct primes, impossible with only 2, 3, and 5 available. The attainable minimum is b = 768, with digit sum 21, choice E.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded, faithful adaptation of MAA Solution 19 on pages 10 and 11. It retains the coprime-ratio and disjoint-prime-factor argument while making the small-denominator exclusions explicit.
review.annotationCheck: Positivity follows from r = b/720 > 1, so no sign case is omitted. The minimality proof is reconstructible at AMC 10 level, and the selected concepts match it.
